cards.text: It's the first day of the week, that very evening. The disciples are together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews. Locked TIGHT, friend, like a cookie box I just sealed.

cards.question: With the disciples' doors locked, Jesus comes and stands among them.

cards.text: Jesus stands right there among them and says, 'Peace be with you!' Friend, if that were me, I'd have jumped so high my gold base would've hit the ceiling.

cards.question: Jesus is standing among the disciples in that locked room. What does He show them?

answers.text: The linen cloths from the tomb

cards.question: The disciples ___ when they saw the Lord.

cards.text: Again Jesus says, 'Peace be with you.' That's twice now, and the dead batteries I shared a drawer with never ONCE wished each other peace.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that the Father has sent Him. So what does Jesus say He is doing with the disciples?

answers.text: He is telling them to wait

cards.text: Then Jesus leans in and breathes on them. Quiet moment, friend. Let it sit.

cards.question: Jesus has just breathed on the disciples. What does He tell them to receive?
Then Jesus talks to the disciples about forgiveness. If they forgive anyone his sins, they are ___. If they withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is ___.

cards.text: Now meet Thomas, called Didymus, one of the Twelve, and he was not with the disciples when Jesus came. Of ALL the nights to miss, friend. OF ALL THE NIGHTS.
So the other disciples tell him, 'We have seen the Lord!' Biggest news the group chat has ever had, and Thomas missed the meeting.

cards.question: Thomas believes the other disciples right away when they tell him they have seen the Lord.
What does Thomas say he needs before he will believe the Lord is alive?

answers.text: To see and touch His wounds
To see the empty tomb himself

cards.text: Eight days later, the disciples are inside AGAIN with the doors locked, and this time Thomas is with them. Jesus comes and stands among them and says, 'Peace be with you.'

cards.question: Jesus turns to Thomas. What does Jesus tell Thomas to do?

answers.text: Touch His hands and His side
Kneel down and pray for faith

cards.text: Then Jesus tells him, 'Stop doubting and believe.' Thomas told the OTHER disciples exactly what he needed, and Jesus offers him that very thing.

cards.question: Jesus has offered Thomas His hands and His side. What does Thomas say to Jesus?

cards.text: Jesus tells Thomas he has believed because he has seen Him. Then Jesus talks about people who were never in that room.

cards.question: Jesus tells Thomas that blessed are those who have not ___ and yet have ___.

cards.text: Then the writer steps back and talks about the signs Jesus performed in the presence of His disciples. Friend, this is the part where the book turns around and looks right at you.

cards.question: Every sign Jesus performed in front of His disciples is written in this book.
The book says why these signs were written down. What is the reason?

answers.text: So you may believe and have life
So the temple keeps a record

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is NOT done yet.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of the story ('that very evening' after the empty tomb and Mary Magdalene's report). The opening card never says that Jesus has risen or what happened earlier that day, so the baker doesn't know why the disciples are hiding or why Jesus appearing matters.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke mixes two pictures. 'Biggest news the group chat has ever had' is the modern comparison, and 'Thomas missed the meeting' is the gathering in the story. The comparison and the Bible setting are blended into one line.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'People who were never in that room' changes what Jesus says. In 20:29 He speaks of 'those who have not seen.' Not being in the room is not the same thing: Mary Magdalene was not in the room but had seen the Lord (20:18). The retelling adds a meaning the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'This is the part where the book turns around and looks right at you' points ahead to 'so that you may believe' in 20:31. That gives away card 13's answer: only the right answer is about 'you', and the line rules out the temple and disciples answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites only John 20:30, but its second sentence draws on 20:31 (the book speaking to 'you'). The citation is narrower than what the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'And that's where we'll leave it for now.', is copied word for word from the doc's example line. It should be a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, which the docs allow because 20:31 is asked on card 13. The card still cites John 20:31, even though it tells no verse.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, what should its 'verses' field cite: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or something else?
